title: Fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions
subtitle: Translate between representations and model quantitative relationships with confidence.

isi: Fractions, decimals, and percentages describe the same part-to-whole relationship in different forms. Before performing a calculation, simplify and keep the numerator and denominator connected to their meaning.

isi.title: Worked example
isi.content: To simplify \(\frac{11}{5}\div\frac{2}{5}\), multiply by the reciprocal: \(\frac{11}{5}\cdot\frac{5}{2}=\frac{11}{2}\).

isi: Choose the form that makes the question easiest to read. A decimal becomes a percent by multiplying by 100, while a percent becomes a decimal by dividing by 100.
Identify the whole before calculating. The basic model is part = percent × whole, where the percentage is written as a decimal.

isi.title: Worked example
isi.content: If \(18\) is what percent of \(90\), write \(18=\frac{p}{100}(90)\). Dividing by \(90\) gives \(p=20\), so the answer is \(20\%\).

isi: Percent change compares the change with the original amount. The original value is the denominator, even when the new value is larger or smaller.

items.title: Discount
items.content: Multiply by \(1-r\). A 20% discount uses factor \(0.80\).

items.title: Tax or growth
items.content: Multiply by \(1+r\). A 7% tax uses factor \(1.07\).

items.title: Sequential changes
items.content: Multiply factors. Do not simply add or subtract the percentages.

isi.title: Discount followed by tax
isi.content: A USD 100 sweater discounted by 20% and taxed at 7% costs \(100(0.80)(1.07)=\text{USD }85.60\).
A 10% increase followed by a 10% decrease does not return to the original value: \(1.10\cdot0.90=0.99\), so the final amount is 1% lower.

isi: A ratio \(a:b\) describes two quantities in a fixed order. Represent the quantities as \(ak\) and \(bk\), where \(k\) is the common scale factor.

isi.title: Ratio model
isi.content: If girls to boys is \(2:5\), then \(G=2k\) and \(B=5k\). If there are 28 girls, \(2k=28\), so \(k=14\) and \(B=70\).
The total number of parts is \(2+5=7\). If the total is known, divide the total by 7 before finding each group.

materi.judul: Rates, direct variation, and inverse variation
isi: Rates compare quantities with different units. Convert units first, then use the rate. For variation questions, decide whether the product or the quotient stays constant.

rows: The rate for one unit of time

isi.title: Worked example
isi.content: A student writes 5 pages in 20 minutes. In 5 hours, there are 300 minutes. The rate is \(\frac{5}{20}=\frac14\) page per minute, so the student writes \(300\cdot\frac14=75\) pages.

items: Name the whole, part, original value, and new value.
Preserve the order of a ratio exactly as stated.
Use compatible units before applying a rate.
Use a factor below 1 for a discount or decrease and above 1 for tax, growth, or increase.
Estimate before calculating so an unreasonable result is easy to catch.

latihan.question: Simplify \(\frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{8}\).
Convert \(0.36\) to a fraction and a percent.
discussion: Write \(0.36=\frac{36}{100}\) and simplify by dividing by 4.

latihan.question: A jacket priced at USD 80 is discounted by 15%. What is the sale price?
discussion: A 15% discount leaves 85% of the original price.
Calculate \(80(0.85)=68\), so the sale price is USD 68.

latihan.question: The ratio of red to blue marbles is \(3:4\). If there are 12 red marbles, how many blue marbles are there?
discussion: Multiply the blue part by the same factor: \(4\cdot4=16\).

latihan.question: A population increases from 2,500 to 2,875. What is the percent increase?
Twelve workers complete a task in 15 days. Assuming inverse variation, how many days would 20 workers need?
discussion: For inverse variation, workers × days stays constant.

latihan.question: Fractions Quiz: Simplify \(\frac{2}{5}+\frac{4}{15}\).
Fractions Quiz: Simplify \(\frac{3}{7}-\frac{1}{0.5}\).
Fractions Quiz: Simplify \(\frac{2}{7}\times\frac{14}{3}\).
Fractions Quiz: Simplify \(\frac{11}{5}\div\frac{2}{5}\).
Complete the percentage conversion table: \(0.75\), \(12\%\), and \(\frac{3}{5}\). Give each as a decimal, fraction, and percent.
discussion: Convert decimals to percentages by multiplying by 100 and percentages to decimals by dividing by 100.

latihan.question: \(25\) is what percent of \(40\)?
discussion: Divide the part by the whole: \(25\div40=0.625\).

latihan.question: \(18\) is what percent of \(90\)?
discussion: Solving gives \(p=20\), so the answer is \(20\%\).

latihan.question: \(10\) is \(50\%\) of what number?
A book was on sale for 40% off its original price. If the sale price was USD 18.00, what was the original price?
discussion: A 40% discount leaves 60% of the original price.

latihan.question: During a sale, a sweater listed at USD 100 is discounted by 20% and then taxed at 7%. How much did Arianna pay?
The sum of three numbers is \(855\). One number, \(x\), is 50% more than the sum of the other two numbers. What is \(x\)?
discussion: Let the sum of the other two numbers be \(s\). Then \(x=1.5s\).

latihan.question: Becca deposits USD 100 in an account earning 4% annual compound interest. How many years will it take to increase the account value by at least 60%?
discussion: The target value is USD 160, so solve \(100(1.04)^t\ge160\).
Testing the choices, \(1.04^{12}\approx1.601\), so 12 years is the first choice to reach at least 60% growth.

latihan.question: An account earns 2% interest compounded annually. The value after \(t\) years is modeled by \(100(x)^t\). What is \(x\)?
discussion: A 2% annual increase uses the growth factor \(1+0.02\).

latihan.question: The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 12 girls, how many boys are there?
The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 50 boys, how many girls are there?
The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 35 students in the class, how many boys are there?
discussion: There are 7 total ratio parts, so each part is \(35\div7=5\).

latihan.question: The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 4 girls, how many students are there?
The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 28 girls, what is the difference between the number of girls and boys?
discussion: The scale factor is \(28\div2=14\), so there are \(5\times14=70\) boys.

latihan.question: The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 21 more boys than girls, how many boys are there?
The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If the difference between the number of girls and boys is 15, what is the total number of students?
The ratio of girls to boys is \(2:5\). If there are 21 students in total, what is the difference between the number of girls and boys?
If a student writes 2 pages per 3 minutes, how many minutes does it take to write 180 pages?
discussion: The time per page is \(3\div2=1.5\) minutes.

latihan.question: If a student writes 5 pages per 20 minutes, how many pages can the student write in 5 hours?
discussion: The rate is \(5\div20=\frac14\) page per minute, so \(300\times\frac14=75\).

latihan.question: If a student writes 80 pages in 20 minutes, what is the writing rate?
discussion: Rate is quantity divided by time: \(80\div20=4\).

latihan.question: An acidic solution has a nitric acid-to-water mass ratio of \(2:7\). If the total mass is 270 grams, how many more grams of water are there than nitric acid?
discussion: There are 9 parts, so each part is \(270\div9=30\) grams.
Water is 210 grams and acid is 60 grams, giving a difference of \(210-60=150\) grams.

latihan.question: Nate walks 25 meters in 13.7 seconds. At the same rate, which distance is closest to what he walks in 4 minutes?
discussion: Calculate \(25\div13.7\times240\approx438\) meters, which is closest to 450 meters.

latihan.question: A rectangular reproduction has dimensions one-third the original. If the original height is 29 inches, what is the reproduction's height?
discussion: Multiply the original height by the scale factor: \(29\times\frac13=\frac{29}{3}\) inches.

latihan.question: A baker needs 2.5 ounces of chocolate per muffin. How many pounds are needed for 48 muffins? Use 1 pound = 16 ounces.
The time to consume a buffalo carcass is inversely proportional to the number of vultures. If 12 vultures take 3 days, how many fewer hours will it take with 16 vultures?
discussion: With 16 vultures, the time is \(36\div16=2.25\) days, or 18 hours less than 3 days.

latihan.question: The ratio of boys to girls is \(x:y\). If the total number of children is five times the number of boys, which could be the sum of \(x+y\)?
discussion: The simplest integer ratio is \(x:y=1:4\), whose sum is 5. Any equivalent ratio has sum a multiple of 5, so 10 could be the sum.

latihan.question: A miniature's scale is 0.4 inches to 1 foot of actual height. If Gary is 5 feet 9 inches tall, what is the miniature's height?
Wyatt can husk between 12 and 18 dozen ears of corn per hour. What is a possible amount of time, in hours, to husk 72 dozen ears?
latihan.answer: Any time from 4 to 6 hours; for example, 5 hours.
discussion: At 18 dozen per hour, the time is \(72\div18=4\) hours.
At 12 dozen per hour, the time is \(72\div12=6\) hours, so any time in the interval \([4,6]\) is possible.

latihan.question: A television station sells time slots in 30-minute intervals and operates 24 hours per day. How many slots can it sell for Tuesday and Wednesday?
discussion: Two days contain 48 hours, and each hour contains two 30-minute intervals.

latihan.question: One ounce of graphene can cover 7 football fields, and each field is approximately \(1\frac13\) acres. About how many acres can 48 ounces cover?

additionalPractice.question: Find 25% of 72.
A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. At the same rate, how far will it travel in 4.5 hours?
discussion: The rate is \(180\div3=60\) miles per hour.

additionalPractice.question: A mixture has acid to water ratio \(2:7\) and total mass 270 grams. How many grams of water are present?
discussion: There are \(2+7=9\) total parts, so each part is \(270\div9=30\) grams.

additionalPractice.question: A price is increased by 10% and then decreased by 10%. Is the final price equal to the original price?
additionalPractice.answer: No; the final price is 1% less than the original.
discussion: The final price is \(99\%\) of the original, so it is 1% lower.

additionalPractice.question: A recipe uses 2 cups of flour for 4 cookies. How many cups are needed for 30 cookies?
discussion: The recipe uses \(2\div4=\frac12\) cup per cookie.

additionalPractice.question: One quantity is 40% less than \(x\), while another is 50% greater than \(x\). What is the ratio of the first quantity to the second?
discussion: The first quantity is \(0.60x\), and the second is \(1.50x\).

additionalPractice.question: Simplify \(\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{8}\).
discussion: The denominators match, so add the numerators: \(\frac{3}{8}+\frac{1}{8}=\frac{4}{8}=\frac12\).

additionalPractice.question: Convert \(0.45\) to a percent.
The ratio of cats to dogs is \(2:3\). If there are 8 cats, how many dogs are there?
A car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. What is its average rate?
discussion: Average rate is distance divided by time: \(180\div3=60\) miles per hour.

additionalPractice.question: A jacket priced at USD 120 is discounted by 25%. What is the sale price?
discussion: A 25% discount leaves 75% of the price.

additionalPractice.question: The ratio of boys to girls is \(3:4\). If there are 35 students, how many are girls?
discussion: There are 7 parts, so each part is \(35\div7=5\).

additionalPractice.question: A recipe uses 3 cups of flour for 8 servings. How many cups are needed for 20 servings?
discussion: The rate is \(3\div8\) cups per serving.

additionalPractice.question: A quantity increases from 80 to 104. What is the percent increase?
discussion: The increase is 24. Relative to the original: \(24\div80=0.30=30\%\).

additionalPractice.question: Twelve workers finish a job in 10 days. Assuming inverse variation, how many days would 15 workers need?
A price is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the final price of an item that originally cost USD 250?
The ratio of red paint to blue paint is \(5:2\). If 21 liters of mixture are used, how many liters are red paint?
discussion: There are 7 parts, so each part is \(21\div7=3\) liters.

additionalPractice.question: A machine produces 240 parts in 8 hours. Its production rate increases by 25%. How many parts will it produce in 10 hours at the new rate?
discussion: The original rate is \(240\div8=30\) parts per hour.
The new rate is \(30(1.25)=37.5\), so 10 hours produces \(375\) parts.

additionalPractice.question: A solution contains acid and water in the ratio \(3:7\). How many grams of water must be added to 200 grams of solution to make the ratio \(1:3\)?
discussion: The initial acid is \(\frac{3}{10}(200)=60\) grams and water is 140 grams.
For a 1:3 ratio, 60 grams of acid requires 180 grams of water, so add \(180-140=40\) grams.

additionalPractice.question: A car travels the first half of a trip at 40 miles per hour and the second half at 60 miles per hour. What is the average speed for the entire trip?
discussion: For equal distances, use total distance divided by total time, not the arithmetic mean.
The harmonic mean is \(\frac{2(40)(60)}{40+60}=48\) miles per hour.

additionalPractice.question: A student answers 80% of the first 25 questions correctly. How many of the next 15 must be correct to have at least 70% accuracy after 40 questions?
discussion: At least 70% of 40 is 28, so at least \(28-20=8\) of the next 15 must be correct.

additionalPractice.question: A quantity \(x\) varies directly with \(y\). When \(y=6\), \(x=15\). What is \(x\) when \(y=14\)?
A quantity \(x\) varies inversely with \(y\). When \(y=8\), \(x=15\). What is \(x\) when \(y=12\)?
A store marks up an item by 40% and then gives a 15% discount. Compared with the original price, the final price is:
discussion: The final price is 19% greater than the original.

additionalPractice.question: A tank contains 140 liters after 4 minutes and 260 liters after 10 minutes. If it is filled at a constant rate, what was the initial amount of water?
discussion: The rate is \((260-140)\div(10-4)=20\) liters per minute.
Four minutes added 80 liters, so the initial amount was \(140-80=60\) liters.
